commits.subject: docs(roadmap): show the AJC completed cones and name the real build-cost driver
commits.summary: The condensed roadmap now mirrors the structured tree: the substrate, line-bundle, Grassmannian/graded and Čech cones are listed as done with their named sub-items, and the maintenance bullet states the measured root cause of build cost — the bare `import Mathlib` in 86 of 164 modules, not the heartbeat budgets.

commits.subject: blueprint(ajc): restore 1,123 statement titles that LaTeX was swallowing into the body
commits.summary:
**The bug.** 1,123 of the 1,592 titled nodes were written `\begin{lemma}\leanok[Title]`. LaTeX scans an environments optional argument immediately after `\begin{lemma}`, so the intervening `\leanok` ended the scan and the bracketed phrase fell into the statement body: the built site rendered 1,108 nodes with their name as stray literal `[...]` text and no title at all. Every occurrence is now `\begin{lemma}[Title]\leanok`.

**Content-preserving.** Verified mechanically across all 29 chapters: non-whitespace character count, `\begin{` count and `\leanok` count are byte-identical before and after; the only other effect is that multi-line titles are joined onto one line. Zero residual `\leanok[` occurrences remain.

commits.subject: docs(AJC): correct README/TO_USER to measured state; make analogies, informal and memory honest indexes
commits.summary:
**Corrected a mathematical misstatement.** The README described the target as the Jacobian of a geometrically *integral* curve; `AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean` states it for a smooth, proper, geometrically *irreducible* curve. Also replaced the invented cone list ("Serre-finiteness, Quot, Picard-identity-component") with the roadmap names that exist: closed `AJC.substrate`/`AJC.linebundle`/`AJC.grquot`/`AJC.cech`, open `AJC.fbc`/`AJC.rr`/`AJC.picrep`/`AJC.pic0av`/`AJC.albanese`.

**Replaced unquantified prose with the measured state:** 164 modules and 121,662 lines, exactly 24 `sorry` in 11 modules (so 153 of 164 sorry-free), a warm green build of 8,723 jobs with 162 warning heads over 28 files, and 86 of 164 modules opening with a bare `import Mathlib` (132 inheriting one transitively). `TO_USER.md` stays at three bullets; its claim that the residual build cost is "bounded heartbeat, synthesis, and import audits" is corrected to name the umbrella import as the measured root cause.

**`analogies/` is now an honest index rather than a topic list.** Its old closing sentence said the `rigidity`/`cotangent`/`differential` notes "cover the Picard identity component"; they in fact cover the genus-0 lane deleted on 2026-06-23. 47 of the 123 notes (872 KB, ~47%) are written against ten modules verified to have zero occurrences left under `AlgebraicJacobian/`, and the README now gives the grep that identifies them, the iteration-band rule for the rest, and the mtime caveat that 107 notes share one bulk-import timestamp.

**`memory/` and `informal/` classified per entry.** In `memory/`, `d3-split-landed.md` and `ts225-blueprint-audit.md` are marked superseded (`PullbackTensorComp.lean` no longer exists; `rationalMap_to_av_extends` has zero references against nine for `extend_to_av`). `informal/` gains an index: the two `projectiveLineBar_*` notes are dead (`ProjectiveLineBar`: zero references), while `tensorObj_restrict_iso` and `exists_tensorObj_inverse` are stale *journals* whose declarations are live (87 and 39 references) — so the journal retires, not the mathematics. Nothing was deleted.

commits.subject: fix(scripts): delimit the import header structurally, not by the last line starting with import
commits.summary: **Bug.** The probe inserted `#import_bumps` after the last line beginning with `import `, which in Cohomology/RegroupHelper.lean is prose inside the module docstring ("import boundary, enabling ..."). The macro landed inside a comment, the linter never fired, and the module was silently reported as unconvertible. The scanner now walks comment blocks, blanks and real `import M` lines from the top and stops at the first command, which is where Lean itself ends the header.

commits.summary: **Attribution fix.** 138 of 164 files carried `Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Merten` / `Authors: Christian Merten`, copied from the seed statement file `references/challenge.lean`. commits.subject: build(ajc): drive the import-hygiene campaign wave by wave over the import DAG
commits.summary: **Why waves.** A modules minimal-import probe is only correct once its whole transitive project-import closure is umbrella-free: while a dependency still says `import Mathlib` it hands the entire library to the importer, and the `linter.minImports` pass then reports every Mathlib module as redundant. Each wave therefore converts exactly the bare modules whose project dependencies are already clean, rebuilds them so the next waves probes see the narrowed oleans, and repeats. Wave 1 is the 27 DAG sources.

commits.subject: build(ajc): add the de-umbrella and budget-trim tooling for the import-hygiene campaign
commits.summary:
**Why.** 86 of 164 modules open with a bare `import Mathlib`; 27 of them are DAG sources, so 132 of 164 modules transitively load the full 8,171-module Mathlib environment. Measured during the cold build now running: each such Lean process peaks at 6.8--7.0 GB RSS, which caps effective parallelism on a 16-core/62 GB host at about 8 jobs.

**Tooling.** `scripts/min-imports.sh` runs Mathlibs `#import_bumps` (the `linter.minImports` linter) on a throwaway copy and reports the precise imports a module needs; `scripts/deumbrella.sh` rewrites the import block and re-elaborates with `lake env lean`, restoring the original on any failure so the tree is never left broken; `scripts/trim-budgets.sh` does the same for `maxHeartbeats` / `synthInstance.maxHeartbeats` / `maxRecDepth` scopes. None of them touches `.lake/build`.

commits.subject: roadmap(ajc): make the finished mathematics visible as 30 done sub-items
commits.summary:
**Completed side made explicit.** The AJC tree recorded ~153 sorry-free Lean modules behind four opaque `done` nodes. Each of `AJC.substrate`, `AJC.cech`, `AJC.grquot`, `AJC.linebundle`, `AJC.rr`, `AJC.albanese`, `AJC.picrep` now carries named sub-items — scheme/sheaf substrate, relative Spec, descent, tangent spaces, rigidity, genus; the Čech engine, identification, acyclicity, pushPull, Mayer--Vietoris and the comparison theorem; Grassmannian cells, graded rings, Hilbert--Serre, flattening, generic flatness; line-bundle coherence, pullback, tensor, dual and the Picard group law; the adelic Riemann--Roch lane; Auslander--Buchsbaum and the rational-map substrate; the rigidified pushforward engine and Quot base change.

**Every citation checked.** All 120 module paths named in the new summaries exist, and none of them is one of the 11 modules that still carry a `sorry` (24 in total), so each `done` label is backed by a sorry-free module set.
